title: Gaussian extremality for weighted relative Fisher information at fixed mean and covariance

fisher_extremality.density_and_score: Let mu=N(0,I_d), let nu=rho mu have mean m, positive covariance S and weak score u=grad log rho with finite weighted relative Fisher information I_Omega=E_nu[u^T Omega u]
fisher_extremality.score_identities: Gaussian integration by parts gives E_nu u=m and E_nu[(X-m)(u-m)^T]=S-I
fisher_extremality.matrix_regression: Matrix Cauchy, equivalently positivity of the residual after regressing u-m on X-m, gives Cov_nu(u)>=(S-I)S^(-1)(S-I)
fisher_extremality.sharp_bound: I_Omega(nu|mu)>=m^T Omega m+Tr[Omega(S+S^(-1)-2I)] for every positive Omega
fisher_extremality.equality: Equality holds exactly when u-m=(I-S^(-1))(X-m), whose normalized solution is the Gaussian N(m,S)
fisher_extremality.wavefunction: For psi=sqrt(rho) exp(i theta), q0[psi]=(1/4)I_Omega(nu|mu)+int |grad theta|_Omega^2 dnu, so phase cannot lower the cost and the positive Gaussian amplitude is the unique fixed-moment minimizer up to constant phase
fisher_extremality.closure: Smooth positive densities prove the identities directly; standard Gaussian convolution and lower semicontinuity extend the bound to finite-Fisher densities with positive covariance
fisher_extremality.scope_guard: The theorem prices every non-Gaussian density by its first two moments but supplies no lower bound on its Wick-square expectation from those moments alone
